newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end up, extend winning run.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end up, extend winning run.

text.p: The Australian share market closed confidently higher on Friday with the presence of afternoon buyers ensuring the local bourse extended its winning run to four consecutive positive finishes.
By the close, the All Ordinaries index had climbed 9.6 points to 2283.0.
After reaching a seven week low of 2213.4 on Tuesday, the benchmark All Ordinaries index has climbed 69.6 points or 3.14 percent to its September month's high so far.
Turnover topped A$1.33 billion as a result of the exercise of options after Thursday's expiry, with about A$700 million of trade through the market pre-opening.
Brokers said solid buying interest had underpinned the strength seen today.
"It's behaved itself quite well and gathered momentum as the day progressed," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at brokerage Intersuisse.
While Sekely noted the looming September SPI contract expiry on Monday, he said the buying interest appeared real with its timing suggesting Asian investors had stepped into the market.
"It could be artifical but it has the feel of genuine buying and the timing zone difference suggests it could be Asian buying," Sekely said.

Features remained scarce in a broadly strong market but Orbital Engine shares jumped over 13 percent after the company announced a deal to supply the Indonesian national car project with its combustion process engine.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
